label: Born in Brussels
description: Born on New Year's Eve 1514 into a wealthy family of physicians and pharmacists.

sources.quote: Andreas Vesalius was born on New Year's Eve 1514 in Brussels, Brabant, into a wealthy family of physicians and pharmacists.

label: Early education at University of Louvain
description: Included instruction in rhetoric, philosophy, logic, and classical languages.

sources.quote: His early education at the Castle School of the University of Louvain included instruction in rhetoric, philosophy, logic, and classical languages (Latin, Greek, and Hebrew).

label: Moved to Paris
description: Went to Paris to study anatomy.

sources.quote: Shortly thereafter, his interest turned to medicine, and he went to Paris to study anatomy.

label: Returned to University of Louvain
description: Returned to finish studies in medicine when Charles V declared war on France.

sources.quote: When Charles V declared war on France 3 years later, in 1536, Vesalius returned to the University of Louvain to finish his studies in medicine, receiving the degree of licentiate (equivalent to a master's degree).

label: Presented thesis Paraphrasis in nonum librum Rhaeze
description: A paraphrase of the ninth book of Rhazae about the Arabic pharmacology.

sources.quote: He presented a thesis titled "Paraphrasis in nonum librum Rhaeze" (Leuven, Rutgerus Rescuis, 1537), a paraphrase of the ninth book of Rhazae about the Arabic pharmacology.

label: Published thesis in Basel
description: Published the thesis again a month later in Basel.

sources.quote: He was not pleased with the printing and published it again a month later in Basel.

label: Moved to Padua
description: Moved to the capital of the scientific Renaissance to pursue medicine and anatomy.

sources.quote: Thereafter, Vesalius moved to the capital of the scientific Renaissance, Padua, Italy, to pursue his passion for medicine and anatomy.

label: Received doctorate of medicine
description: Received doctorate and was nominated as a professor.

sources.quote: By December 1537, he received his doctorate of medicine and was nominated as a professor.

label: Appointed professor at Padua
description: Worked as a professor of surgery and anatomy, succeeding Paolo Colombo.

sources.quote: He worked there as a professor of surgery and anatomy, succeeding Paolo Colombo from Cremona.

label: Published Tabulae Sex
description: Publication of 6 anatomical tables, his first known hand-drawn anatomical work.

sources.quote: His observations eventually led to the publication of 6 anatomical tables, the Tabulae Sex, in 1538.

label: Compared monkey and human skeleton
description: Found a process of the lumbar vertebrae in the monkey that was not present in the human, realizing Galen's error.

sources.quote: In a startling experiment in 1541, Vesalius put the skeleton of a monkey and the skeleton of a human, side by side.

label: Published De Humani Corporis Fabrica
description: Published his dissections and sketches in the most influential text, De Humani Corporis Fabrica Libri Septem.

sources.quote: Vesalius published his dissections and sketches in the most influential text: De Humani Corporis Fabrica Libri Septem (The Structure of the Human Body).

label: Appointed Imperial Physician
description: Secured the position of Imperial Physician, serving until Charles V abdicated.

sources.quote: The publication of Fabrica also helped Vesalius secure the position of Imperial Physician, in which he served until Charles V abdicated in 1556.

label: Charles V abdicated
description: Charles V abdicated, ending Vesalius's service as Imperial Physician.

sources.quote: The publication of Fabrica also helped Vesalius secure the position of Imperial Physician, in which he served until Charles V abdicated in 1556.
